newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Liebscher against watered-down EMU.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Liebscher against watered-down EMU.

text.p: Austrian National Bank president Klaus Liebscher said on Thursday he was against any watering down of the convergence criteria for Europe's planned single currency, the euro.
"I am against the sometimes voiced proposals to water down or politically soften the criteria," Liebscher said in a statement.
"That would lead to a risk premium for the euro above all in longer-dated yields which would affect all participating countries and all debtors in those countries," he said.
The central banker said he was also against a postponement of the single currency.
"A postponement of EMU (Economic and Monetary Union) carries with it the danger that all the confidence built up in the markets, above all in the last year, could be undermined," he said.

Austria was already well placed to qualify for the single currency, with a low inflation rate, a stable currency and a cost-cutting budget that should steer the budget deficit within three percent of GDP by the end of 1997.

According to a Reuters survey of 45 economists across Europe, released on Thursday, Austria was forecast by all but one of the economists as a first-wave starter for the single currency. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 256
